answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it can claim work or vote, then slash that stake when bonded counterparties prove fraud through signed, auditable transaction records. Creating a thousand aliases does not multiply influence for free: each must tie up capital, and collusion risks losing it. A raven may flag a suspicious cluster, but only verifiable evidence triggers slashing; zephyr and falcon identities face the same rule. This raises Sybil attacks from cheap account creation to a costly, attributable gamble.
